title: Diagonal split-torus action on polynomial projective space over a ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $r,n\in\mathbb N$. Let $T=D_A(\mathbb Z^r)$ be the split torus with its specified Laurent Hopf structure [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group], and put $C=A[\mathbb Z^r]$. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}A[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ with total-degree grading and its structure morphism to $S$ [def-pc-proj] [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Given weights $w_i\in\mathbb Z^r$, define the ring homomorphism $\rho_w:A[z_0,\ldots,z_n]\to C[z_0,\ldots,z_n]$ by $\rho_w(a)=a$ and $\rho_w(z_i)=t^{w_i}z_i$. An $S$-action $a:T\times_SP\to P$ on schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-fibre-product], with the unit and associativity identities, is the diagonal projective action with weights $w$ if it is induced by $\rho_w$ on homogeneous coordinates. Precisely, $\rho_w$ and the coefficient inclusion have graded lifts $\varphi,\psi$ with the irrelevant-ideal condition for their Proj maps, and there is an isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Proj}C[z_0,\ldots,z_n]\xrightarrow{\sim}T\times_SP$ whose composites with the projections are respectively the standard morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $\operatorname{Proj}(\psi)$, and such that $a\circ e=\operatorname{Proj}(\varphi)$. Both projection equalities fix $e$ uniquely. No nonzero-ring, reducedness or positive-rank hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Thomason (1987), Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4(3), printed p.32; the explicit split-torus diagonal homogeneous-coordinate specialization formulated in the parent node. Polynomial Proj and its base change as in Stacks Constructions, Tags 01ND and 01OE.
